heading: INT. CURLING CLUB - SALT MINE LEVEL TWO - NIGHT

units.text: INT. CURLING CLUB - SALT MINE LEVEL TWO - NIGHT
A sheet of ice laid inside a hollowed-out salt chamber, lit by work lamps strung from the ceiling.
The walls glitter pink and white.
Stones sit in their rack like sleeping animals.
HOLLIS BRANNIGAN, 60s, barrel-chested, a cardigan under his club blazer, kneels at the far hog line with a pebble can.
He sprays the ice in careful rows, one pass, then another.
He has done this alone for a long time.
A steel door clangs somewhere above.
Footsteps on the stairs.
Hollis does not look up.
He sprays another row.
TAMSIN OKAFOR, late 20s, tall, hair still wet from a shower, enters with her broom over her shoulder and a duffel dragging from her other hand.
She stops at the hack.
She sets the duffel down, picks it up again, sets it down.
Hollis sprays.
She watches the back of his head, then crouches and runs a glove along the ice as if checking it for a fever.
Ice is fast tonight.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: It's always fast when it doesn't matter.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Hollis caps the can.
He stands in two stages, hand on his knee, and walks the length of the sheet to the rack.
Tamsin slides into the hack without a stone, her eyes on the button, her broom across her lap.
Hollis lifts a stone, wipes the running band with his sleeve, and carries it back to her.
He sets it beside her boot.
Neither speaks.
A drip of brine lands somewhere in the dark.
They called at six.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: I heard.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Eleven years.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Thirty-one, for the building.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: She almost laughs and turns it into a cough.
He pulls the stone's handle straight, a quarter-inch adjustment that does nothing.
You could have told me before the bonspiel.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Would you have thrown it differently?
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: She says nothing.
She takes the handle, sets her feet, and slides out, long and low.
The stone runs down the sheet in a clean curl.
Hollis walks beside it, not sweeping, hands in his blazer pockets, and when it stops a foot short of the button he nods at it the way a man nods at a stranger on a train.
Short.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Mm.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: He bends, picks up the stone, and carries it back himself.
She lets him.
At the hack he sets it down again beside her boot, exactly where it was before, and straightens the broom on her lap so the brush points the right way.
Lock up when you're done. The key sticks. Lift, then turn.
units.name: HOLLIS

units.text: Lift, then turn.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: He goes up the stairs one at a time.
At the top the door clangs again.
Tamsin sits in the hack with the stone, in the pink light, and does not throw it.
FADE OUT.
